answers.value: The broker's counter-proposal on an open quote: requested changes to premium, terms, coverage or deductibles; scope = one submission's counter-offer (SUB-####) assessed against the pricing floor, treaty constraints and appetite guidelines in Guidewire PolicyCenter.
During live negotiation, from receipt of the counter-proposal to the revised-quote decision, within the quote's validity window in the current quote cycle.

The assessment records the requested change, the resulting premium versus the technical/filed floor, the impact on terms and any appetite or treaty-capacity breach; every requested concession is priced before a response is given.
The revised premium reconciles to the Earnix rating output for the amended terms (delta = 0); the amended exposure stays within treaty capacity and the risk remains inside documented appetite.

The counter-proposal assessment, rating worksheet and decision are filed in the underwriting file in Guidewire PolicyCenter and OpenText /UW/<submission-no>/quote/ with timestamp and version; retained 7 years.

A counter-proposal below the pricing floor or outside appetite is logged as an exception with disposition (decline / counter at floor / refer to Senior Underwriter for authority) and the rationale recorded before responding.
The assessment uses the current filed rating manual in Earnix and the appetite/authority matrix v3.2; the manual and matrix versions are recorded on the worksheet.
The pricing impact of each requested concession is tested for its effect on the technical premium and target loss ratio; a concession moving the loss ratio beyond the target band triggers referral.
Any concession reducing premium more than 10% below the technical indication, or breaching a treaty capacity limit, is treated as material and referred to the next authority level.
All counter-proposals assessed in the review quarter; a sample of 25 negotiated quotes across personal, commercial and specialty is inspected.

PASS = revised terms priced against the filed manual, within appetite and treaty capacity, with any sub-floor concession referred and approved; FAIL = any quote revised below floor or outside appetite without a documented referral.
A failed assessment is routed to a Senior Underwriter; the quote is re-priced at the floor or declined, and the exception is logged with a rationale and referral record.
Acceptance = counter-proposal fully priced in Earnix, checked against appetite and treaty limits, and any deviation from filed rates authorised per the matrix before the revised quote is issued.
Evidence lands in the Guidewire PolicyCenter underwriting file and OpenText /UW/<submission-no>/quote/ with the assessment, rating worksheet and any referral approval.

answers.value: The quote under negotiation where the broker has cited competing market terms; scope = one submission's price adequacy assessment (SUB-####), comparing our technical premium to the broker's market alternatives while holding rate adequacy.
During the live quote/negotiation window, from receipt of the market-alternative information to the pricing decision, inside the quote validity period in the current cycle.

The assessment records our technical/filed premium, the cited market price, the rate adequacy ratio and the target loss ratio for the class; the technical indication from Earnix is present before any competitive move is considered.

The quoted premium reconciles to the Earnix rating output (delta = 0); the resulting rate adequacy and projected loss ratio are computed and compared to the class target, with any shortfall quantified.

The price-adequacy worksheet, market comparison and decision are filed in the Guidewire PolicyCenter underwriting file and OpenText /UW/<submission-no>/quote/ with timestamp and version; retained 7 years.

A price that would fall below the adequacy floor to match the market is logged as an exception with disposition (hold at technical price / decline / refer for authority) and rationale before responding.
All competitively-negotiated quotes in the review quarter; a sample of 25 across lines where market alternatives were cited is inspected.

PASS = quoted price at or above the adequacy floor with rate adequacy and loss ratio inside target, or a documented referral where matched below floor; FAIL = any quote reduced below the adequacy floor to win business without authority.
A below-floor match is referred to a Senior Underwriter; the quote is held at the technical price or declined, and the exception is logged with the market evidence and referral outcome.

Acceptance = technical premium computed in Earnix, rate adequacy and target loss ratio assessed against class targets, and any competitive reduction authorised per the pricing authority matrix before the quote is confirmed.
Evidence lands in the Guidewire PolicyCenter underwriting file and OpenText /UW/<submission-no>/quote/ with the adequacy worksheet, market comparison and any referral approval.

The approved methodology is the current filed rating manual and the price-adequacy model in Earnix Rating & Pricing (version stated on the worksheet); parameters (loss costs, trend, expense and target loss ratio) are sourced from the pricing actuary's latest signed rate review, cited on the assessment.
